description: A team of curious people exploring space, science, and technology through the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We want to learn, collaborate, and build creative solutions using NASA's open data.
summary:
FlameLens is an interactive research-discovery platform designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research more accessible and understandable.

Addressing the "Flame in Freefall" challenge, FlameLens organizes NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion investigation metadata and available file inventories into a unified interface. Researchers and curious users can explore investigations, search and filter records, inspect research descriptions, discover associated files, analyze inventory distributions, and compare investigations side by side.

The platform combines an interactive dashboard, investigation explorer, file explorer, storage analytics, metadata comparison tools, and an AI-assisted metadata interface.

By reducing the effort required to navigate fragmented research records, FlameLens helps users identify relevant experiments and understand what research resources are available. It provides a foundation for more accessible exploration of combustion science in microgravity while clearly distinguishing available metadata from experimental measurements.
details:
Overview

FlameLens is a web-based research exploration platform developed to support the discovery and understanding of NASA's combustion science investigations, particularly those involving microgravity environments.

The platform addresses the challenge of navigating scientific investigation records and their associated research files by organizing available NASA PSI information into an accessible, interactive experience.

How It Works

FlameLens provides several connected modules:

  1. Research Overview: Presents investigation statistics, file inventory metrics, research categories, and data distributions through an interactive dashboard.
  2. Investigation Explorer: Allows users to search, filter, sort, and inspect NASA PSI combustion investigations.
  3. Investigation Details: Displays available research descriptions, investigation metadata, provenance information, and associated file inventories.
  4. File Explorer: Helps users search and filter available file records by investigation, extension, format, and download status.
  5. Storage Analytics: Visualizes remote inventory sizes, file distributions, and data availability while distinguishing remote inventory from locally downloaded files.
  6. Comparison Studio: Enables side-by-side comparison of investigation metadata and audited file inventories.
  7. AI Assistant: Provides a chat-style interface for exploring questions about available investigation metadata, with support for displaying evidence and citations when returned by the backend.

Technology

The frontend is built using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. The backend uses Python and FastAPI to expose structured API endpoints and serve NASA PSI metadata. The project also uses JSON-based metadata repositories, Docker for containerization, and Git/GitHub for version control.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FlameLens reduces the effort required to discover relevant combustion investigations and understand the research resources associated with them. It provides a centralized starting point for researchers, students, and other users interested in combustion science in microgravity.

The project emphasizes data transparency and scientific integrity by distinguishing available investigation metadata and file inventories from experimental measurements that have not yet been processed.

Creativity and Innovation

Rather than presenting NASA research records as disconnected entries, FlameLens transforms them into an interactive research-discovery experience. Its combination of searchable investigation records, inventory analytics, metadata comparison, and an AI-assisted interface offers multiple ways to explore the available scientific resources.

The team prioritized accessibility, traceability, usability, and accurate representation of the available NASA data.
